AdmissionRefusal.description: Typed deterministic admission refusal retained across the plugin/host boundary.

AdmissionRefusal2.description: Why a round was refused. One refused member admits no member.

AnnotationResolutionReason.description: Why a written entry annotation cannot describe boundary data.

ArtifactName.description: One artifact, by the store that holds it and its reference there.

ArtifactReferrerKind.description: The referrer kinds, as the `referrer_kind` column stores them.

ArtifactStoreId.description: The store that holds an artifact.

oneOf.description: The admitted kernel documents behind the module artifact port.
A process engine's own store, by engine kind.

The immutable process-definition descriptors, keyed by their
`ProcessDefinitionId` (ADR 0113 §3.6). A collectible artifact like the
others: a descriptor lives exactly as long as some referrer holds it.

Retained tool material bundles (K2), held by Run-segment and source
leases until their last dependency ends.

A turn's recorded preparation, by digest, held by the turn journal's
`execution` referrer until the journal cannot replay (FIG-5133).

AttachmentContentMismatch.description: Which claim of a reference its stored content failed.

AttachmentRetentionFailure.description:
Structured attachment failure evidence. Backend diagnostics remain on the
runtime error's message; classification and refusal data remain typed.

oneOf.description: No form the request accepted can carry this attachment.
The stored content disagrees with the reference that names it.

AttachmentRetentionStoreFailure.description:
A nested store cause with the store's authoritative retry class and its
runtime code and structured refusal. The diagnostic is carried separately.

AttachmentStoreFailureClass.description:
Why an attachment-store backend operation failed, as a property a caller can
act on without parsing the message.

The retry and operator verdicts are derived from the class, never stored
separately, so a class and its verdicts cannot contradict each other.

oneOf.description:
The operation may succeed if retried: a transport fault, timeout,
throttling, or an unclassified backend failure.

Credentials or authorization must be corrected before a retry can
succeed; the failure is operator-actionable.

The request, its configuration, or the backend's support for it cannot
succeed as written. Retrying changes nothing.

AwaitEventWaitIdentity.description:
The wait a Deferred source resolves: the deferring tool call it parked
on, by its stable call id (ADR 0117).

BootstrapFault.description: Why a freshly exec'd worker could not take its place on the pipe.

CallableId.description:
A function and its operation context. Authored callbacks retain their defining
Link; build helpers carry the caller's real Link and an exact library ID.

CancelOrigin.description:
The runtime or actor decision that requested cancellation of a process
or of a tool call's attempt. `RunClosing` is a call's owning tool Run
discharging its cancellation at Closing while the turn itself runs on.

CancelRequest.description: A process cancellation fact. Its first timestamp survives retries.

CellConsumption.description: Consumption at a cell decision, from existing kernel and supervisor meters.

consumed.description:
Budget consumed. Charges saturate at the budget; `observed` retains
the raw kernel charge, including the refused crossing unit.
None means Lash has no meter for this bound, or no receipt arrived.

observed.description: The raw meter reading, which can pass the bound.

CellControl.description: The control that ended a cell, as history records it.

oneOf.description:
The turn finished with this value: inline, or retained out of
history when its encoding was too long for it (FIG-1643).
The turn switched to the agent frame `frame_key` names.

CellDefect.description: A rule of a session's cells that a cell's program broke.

oneOf.description: A lexical local makes an offered or deferred operation unreachable.
OP-INTERNAL: an authored unit tried to perform a package-private operation.

The cell used a binding an earlier cell left that held a function or
a task: neither outlives the cell that created it, so the binding
was not carried.

The cell ended with tasks it started and did not await: some still
running, some failed with an error nothing observed. Each is named
by the site that started it and which run of that site it was.

CellFailure.description: Structured failure returned by a code executor.

defect.description:
The rule of a session's cells the program broke, when that is why
the cell failed, kept typed through the plugin and host result.

exec_failure.description:
Why the `exec_code` effect failed before the executor produced a
response, when that is the failure: the closed reason, kept typed
through the protocol driver and the trajectory it records.

feedback.description:
Each pure repair callback's identity and answer, in registration order,
including empty answers. Retained with the failure for replay and attribution.

tool_call_limit.description:
The session's `max_tool_calls` refusal, when that is why the cell
failed (FIG-4546), kept typed through the plugin and host result.

worker_limit.description: The measured run limit, kept typed through the plugin and host result.

CellFailureKind.description: Why an executed code cell failed.

oneOf.description: The runtime refused the program because it violates a dialect or policy bound.
The authored program failed to compile or execute correctly.
Host infrastructure failed while preparing or executing the program.

CellFailureRepair.description: One plugin callback's recorded repair decision for a failed cell.

callback.description: The complete callback key, including its slot prefix.

CellOutcome.description:
What an executed cell resolved to. One of three: a cell never carries a
failure and a control at once, and a cell that finished with `null` is
distinct from one that ran to its end without a control call.

oneOf.description: The cell ran to its end without a control call.
The cell failed.

A declared control call ended the cell: the call of `tool_name`
recorded under `call_id`. The control stays in the record, because
call lists are bounded and pruned.

CellPrint.description:
One print of an executed cell: the text the model read, the value
printed, and how the text was projected from it. The one shape a print
has in the executor's response, in a cell's committed record, in a step's
attachment archive and in the completion activity.

CellResource.description: A cell bound in its native units. Time values use nanoseconds.

CgroupController.description: A cgroup v2 controller a worker's limits need.

CgroupRefusal.description:
Why a pool cannot place its workers in the cgroup v2 subtree its host
named (FIG-6787). The host's deployment, never the run's.

oneOf.description: The subtree is not a cgroup v2 directory.
The subtree cannot hand `controller` to the workers' cgroups.

The subtree refused a worker's cgroup, a limit in it or the worker's
move into it.

CheckFailure.description: One reason, and the node at fault when the fault is in a node.

CheckRefusal.description:
Everything that keeps a document from being admitted. Admission does not
stop at the first fault of the environment: every missing effect, every
mismatched signature and every missing function identity is named.

CheckpointRefusal.description:
Why a checkpoint root's header failed the parent's or the worker's
structural check.

oneOf.description: The root pins another execution closure than its document's.

A page exchange names more than [`crate::PAGE_BATCH_PAGES`] pages or
carries more than [`crate::PAGE_BATCH_BYTES`] envelope bytes.

CompatRefusal.description:
Why a store, an epoch or a stored label is refused.

Each message names its remedy with a `lashctl` command. The JSON shape is
what `lashctl --json` reports and what a newer build reads from an older
one, so a variant's fields change only in place under the version freeze.

oneOf.description:
A SQLite database this build reads but has not migrated: its stamp is
older than the version this build writes. The store's open migrates
every database together, after a complete backup; a component opened
on its own never migrates.

`F` at open: below the writable range (a skipped release) or above it
(a newer fleet).

`F` at open: the store records no fleet epoch. The installer seeds it
and an open never does, so no build decides `F` by opening first.

A SQLite store's configured path is a directory in the retired layout
of three database files (FIG-5195). A SQLite deployment is one
database file (ADR 0132 §12), and formats reset at 1.0, so no release
migrates the old layout: the open refuses it unchanged.

files.description: The retired layout's database files the directory holds.

oneOf.description:
A stable release build refuses a store stamped before 1.0, regardless
of format counters: pre-release shapes changed in place under the freeze.

A stored label this build has no name for (an obligation state or
kind, an attachment owner kind, a referrer kind): a newer build wrote
it. Classified apart from corruption so no pass treats it as absent.

A plugin namespace is stamped with a format the fleet record does not
permit its plugin to write (FIG-4746). Nothing was published.

The fleet record carries no writer range for a plugin (FIG-4746): a
plugin the record does not name publishes only its first format.

A recorded plugin writer range is not a range (FIG-4746). The store
fails closed: no publication of that store is admitted.

A plugin writes no format the fleet record permits it (FIG-4747): an
admission chooses each plugin's writer inside its range, and this
plugin has none there. Nothing was admitted.

ConfigRefusal.description:
A refused config change: the owner it names, where it was refused and
why. Nothing of a refused change is published.

ConfigRefusalReason.description:
Why a config change was refused. Only [`Self::Owner`] carries data in the
owner's registered refusal type; every other reason is the framework's.

oneOf.description: The namespace's stored or requested writer format is unavailable.

The owner refused: `refusal` is its registered refusal type,
serialized, and `message` that refusal's display text.
No installed plugin registers the named owner.
The owner registers no command of the name the site carries.

The session recorded no namespace for the owner, so there is nothing
for the command to change.
A value did not read or write as the owner's type.

ConfigRegistrationError.description: A config registration that cannot stand.

oneOf.description: A factory id must be unique, even if its factory registers no config.

ConfigValueRole.description:
Which value of a config judgment could not be read or written as its
owner's type.

oneOf.description: What a creator stated for the namespace.
A command's arguments.
The options a run stated for the namespace.
The namespace the owner produced: created, reduced or overridden.
A command's output.
The owner's own refusal, which did not encode.

ContractId.description:
What pins an operation's meaning under its signature: opaque text,
compared for equality and never read for anything else.

ControlPhaseExpired.description: An unanswered callback at its host-configured aggregate phase deadline.

DeclarationRefusal.description: Why a declaration, or an outcome under it, is refused.

oneOf.description: A deferring body returned a key other than the source its Run armed.

An isolated call has no inline body, so it cannot declare what only
an inline body returns.

A tool that declares a turn control has no output: its result is
the control alone, so a value without one breaks the declaration.

A Finish's value does not fit the schema its tool declares
([`FinishDeclaration`]), by the same admission as a success's value
([`OutputValueMismatch`](Self::OutputValueMismatch)). The call fails
with no control: it makes no completion candidate, is never
repeated, and its control attempt stays spent.

value_schema.description:
The schema the value was checked against: the admitted
declaration's.

oneOf.description:
A success's value does not fit the output schema its tool's
contract states: it is not an instance of the schema, or does not
decode by the rule a code cell reads the value by (`K-EFF-007`). The
call fails: no caller, model or cell receives the value.

output_schema.description:
The schema the value was checked against: the contract's the
call was admitted under.

DeclaredStartObligationRefusal.description: Why a registration cannot be a declared start.

DefinitionRef.description:
An immutable run definition name and revision a deployment registers.

Resolution looks up the exact revision; a worker that does not serve it
retries and parks, and never falls back to another revision.

Detail.description:
A diagnostic beside a typed cause, cut to [`Self::MAX_BYTES`]. The variant
that carries it decides the class; the bound keeps a refusal within any
frame whatever its text.

EffectOpener.description:
The exact logical opener that durable work binds (ADR 0099 §1).

Run admission records it, recovery validates it, and language host bridges
mint their identities under it. Every path shares the same owner value.

oneOf.description: A turn of a session.

session_id.description: The session the turn belongs to.

oneOf.description:
One operation on a session that runs no turn: a host command, named
by its batch, or the admissions of one shift request.

An operation is a lifecycle owner in the sense §1 means: its id is
durable and retry-stable, so a redrive of the operation binds the
same opener. No logical turn runs under it: every turn a shift runs
is opened by its logical run's [`Turn`](Self::Turn) (FIG-3607
contract 4). A tool-bearing operation Run closes this scope on explicit
completion; tool-free administrative scopes close with their session.

operation_id.description:
The operation's durable identity. A plain string because no one
typed id names every operation; empty is refused, as
`ExecutionScope::validate` refuses an empty scope id.

session_id.description: The session the operation is on.

oneOf.description: One process.

process_id.description: The minted id of the process that owns this work.

EffectRefusal.description:
The refused operation and the controller's own answer (FIG-7426).
This is controller diagnostic text, independent of provider error bodies.

controller_code.description: The controller's code in its own namespace.

detail.description: The controller's diagnostic, bounded by the runtime's error output cut.

effect_kind.description: Stable runtime-effect kind, including kinds authored by newer builds.

EnginePortError.description: Typed refusal, artifact, fence, unsupported or infrastructure error. Infrastructure is never a guest terminal.

oneOf.description: A substrate fault retains its kind and fields across the engine port.
A store refusal retains its structured cause across the engine port.

EntryTypeMismatch.description: A public entry's input or settled result violated its declared contract.

ErrorEnvelope.description:
Structured error payload carried on [`SessionStreamEvent::Error`] (and
[`SessionStreamEvent::RetryStatus`]).

Durability: this type appears inside persisted session snapshots and turn
checkpoints, so every field added after the initial shape must stay
additive — `#[serde(default)]` on decode and
`#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` on encode — to keep
old snapshots decodable and new snapshots readable by older readers.
Transient runtime-stream signal for live consumers.

These events may be partial, duplicated, or display-only and are not proof
of durable session history. Persisted semantic history uses
[`SessionHistoryRecord`].

code.description:
Namespaced failure code: `lash:` codes are this workspace's
[`TurnFailureCode`] vocabulary, everything else is a foreign spelling
carried verbatim and never reinterpreted. A bare spelling decodes as
the pre-cutover form — `lash` when it parses as a `TurnFailureCode`
arm, `provider` otherwise — so old snapshots keep decoding.

effect_refusal.description: The operation and controller answer behind an effect refusal.

kind.description:
Typed origin of the failure. Serializes as the same snake_case string
the field carried when it was a bare `String`, and an unrecognized
spelling decodes as [`TurnFailureKind::Unknown`] rather than failing.

provider_failure_kind.description:
Typed provider-failure classification, set only when the error came
from an LLM provider/transport failure whose kind was classified
(an unclassified `Unknown` kind is surfaced as `None`).

retryable.description:
Whether the failing operation is safe to retry, when the source
carries a typed signal (provider transports classify retryability).
`None` means the source did not know.

Exchange.description: The exchange a worker answered with a message it does not admit.

oneOf.description: The first message of a checkout, which is the handshake.
A step of the run.
The parent was answering the machine's host read.
The parent was answering the machine's page exchange.

ExecCodeFailureReason.description:
Why an `exec_code` effect failed before the executor produced a response.

This is the closed classification offline trace analysis keys on; the human
detail lives in [`ExecCodeFailure::message`]. Serialized snake_case on the
durable journal and trace surfaces.

oneOf.description: No code executor is installed on the session.
The executor's language runtime exited unexpectedly.
Any other session-layer failure; `message` carries the detail.

ExecutionLease.description:
The lease one checkout of a worker runs under. The parent mints it and
fences it when the worker is lost, so a late message under an old lease is
refused rather than applied.

ExecutionScope.description:
Stable semantic identity for one effectful runtime operation.

This is the scope admitted by the host boundary before nondeterministic
work begins. Its journal encoding is an existing durable contract; effect
addresses compose it with a replay key without changing those bytes.

oneOf.description:
One operation on a session that runs no turn: a host command, named
by its batch, or the admissions of one shift request. It has no
logical root, and no logical turn runs under it.

ExportName.description: A document Export, optionally a member of its TypeDef. Type members are not start selectors.

FieldShape.description: One key of an object's shape.

optional.description: Some object merged at this position did not hold the key.

FormatRefusal.description: A plugin cannot interpret or encode this namespace's requested format.

FrameEpoch.description:
The context frame's epoch: advances when a frame opens (F5), which fences
every response from the frame before it.

FrontierRefusal.description: Why a frontier refuses a resolution.

FunctionLocation.description: Source identity before a callable has been linked.

HeaderRefusal.description: Why a receiver refused a header.

HeapFault.description:
A heap fault the worker met itself (FIG-6422), as it crosses to the
parent: infrastructure, never a guest outcome. The wire mirrors the
kernel's `lash_kernel_doc::heap::HeapFault`, which this crate cannot
name: the worker carries each fault's `Display`, which names the page,
as its `detail`.

HelperUnavailableReason.description: Why an exact helper cannot execute on this node.

HookCause.description:
A recorded typed hook cause: a plugin's declared error type, its version
and payload. Unknown payloads survive replay unchanged.

HostPayloadTooLarge.description: A host item refused before durable enqueue or execution.

HostResource.description: The host resources a heap draws on beside guest memory, as they cross.

oneOf.description: Quiescent census bitmap, work-list and root scratch budget.
Resident clean-page cache.
Resident dirty-page budget.
Pages pinned for an activation.
Uncommitted staged page bytes.
One page-read batch.
Host work granted to an activation.

ImportSlot.description: A stable document-local Import coordinate. Names are diagnostic, never dispatch keys.

oneOf.description:
The worker died after it began computing the run, before the run
released it: an end the run may have caused, such as an allocation
abort at the address-space ceiling, a kill for memory or a crash in
a native helper. Another attempt may pass, so it is retryable, but
it spends one of the execution's attempts and is never a capacity
verdict: a run that keeps killing its worker runs out of attempts
(FIG-6786). A worker lost before it computed the run is
[`Self::WorkerCrashed`].

The parent's page service refused the run's page exchange (FIG-6190):
infrastructure, never a guest outcome. The activation ends and its
execution resumes from its last committed root.

A heap fault the worker met itself (FIG-6422): infrastructure,
never a guest outcome. The activation ends and its execution
resumes from its last committed root.

Invalid.description: Why a document or a definition is refused, and the node at fault.

site.description:
The node at fault. `None` when the fault is in no node: the
manifest, an entry, a signature.

oneOf.description:
A library call written as an expression's own call names a
function with no native implementation: a call of it is an
action, `invoke`.

`K-LIB-004`: a library body performs only the operations its
`effects` lists.
`K-LIB-011`: a native version versions a native implementation.
`K-LIB-011`: native versions count from 1.

`K-LIB-003`: a function with a native implementation takes no
function.

`K-LIB-004`: a body that stands beside a native implementation
cannot wait.

`K-EVAL-003`: an assignment evaluates its place before its
right-hand side only when it writes a member, and that right-hand
side is an expression, any action in it nested.

A right-hand side that is one action with variable and literal
arguments is the statement's action, not an expression: the one
spelling kernel text reads back.

`K-CLO-004`: a direct start passes the signature's arguments as the
function's parameters, one for one.
`K-CLO-004`: a token holds its tag first and its callable after it.

IsolatedStartRefusal.description: A process binding that cannot honor admission.

KernelRestoreRefusal.description:
The kernel's precise refusal of a checkpoint it will not resume, carried
typed from the worker to the parent and into the store's graph refusals.

oneOf.description: A live continuation needs an exact build helper absent from this image.

The run's closure lists a function that only a native implements,
and this worker has no native for it.

The run's stored definition of a function is refused at admission:
it is not stored, does not decode, is another function's, is written
for another kernel version, or the checker refuses it. Every
definition a run pins is stored before it parks, so one neither held
nor stored is a store that lost it.

The admission under this execution holds a request of another kind
than the wait's.

KeyRejection.description: A deterministic rejection of a plugin-state key.

LlmCallId.description:
Lash-owned identity for one logical LLM call, spanning all transport
attempts made by the retry owner.

LlmProfileEffortValidationCategory.description:
Deterministic taxonomy of effort-validation failures. The serde snake_case
codes are a stable contract: downstream consumers match on them.

LlmProfileKey.description:
The host's opaque name for one registered model.

Lash never parses it: `glm-5.3-flash@tensorx` names a registration, not a
provider and a model. A session records the key with the metadata the
host's registry minted for it ([`RecordedLlmProfile`]), so the key alone never
decides how a recorded root runs.

MaterialDigest.description:
The integrity digest of the material's canonical bytes: 64 lowercase
hexadecimal digits of a BLAKE3 hash. The hashing domain belongs to the
material codec (FIG-4876), not to this reference.

oneOf.description:
In the owning Run's opener journal: resolvable within the same
segment only.

In a retained artifact store, held by a dependency lease: resolvable
across segments and deployments.

MaterialOwner.description:
Who owns a payload: the logical Run that admitted it, the process that
produced it, or the Deferred source whose seal resolved to it.

oneOf.description: The logical Run, named by its opener.
One process.
One Deferred source, named by its durable wait key.

MaterialRef.description: A typed reference to one canonical payload.

MaterialRefusal.description:
Why recorded material cannot be served: a typed retained-result failure.
None of these re-executes the body that produced the material. FIG-4876
carries it through the runtime error framework.

oneOf.description: No payload exists at the reference's location.

The payload's retention ended; an expired reference cannot restart
work.
The bytes found do not hash to the recorded digest.
The reader's owner is not the reference's owner.

MaterialRole.description:
The record that produced a payload, which is also its sole canonical
owner record: A owns the prepared request, X the attempt output and its
captures, V only presentation bytes distinct from the output.

oneOf.description: The final prepared request admission recorded (A).
One read-only namespace image shared by all admissions at its frontier.

One attempt's output and captures (X), or a cached success a
before-check supplied in its place.
Messages and observations declared by after-checks in D.
Presentation bytes distinct from the output (V).

MaxToolCalls.description:
The number of tool calls one execution may make: the host's required
decision, with no default and no built-in ceiling (FIG-4546).

What it counts depends on the execution. A cell — one code cell of a turn,
or one tool step of a protocol without cells — may make at most this many
tool calls in total. A process may hold at most this many at once: a call
counts from its acceptance until the process no longer depends on it, so
a long-running process is bounded in what it retains, never in what it
does over its life. The call that passes the limit fails with
[`ToolCallLimitExceeded`]; every call under it runs untouched. The limit
paces nothing: rate limits and throttling are the host's own.

oneOf.description:
The runtime's own commit of a turn's input. A host that renders its own
optimistic user row correlates that row to this committed copy through
`turn_id` — typed provenance the runtime publishes — instead of pinning
or parsing a message id. Message ids stay runtime-minted.

input_id.description:
The durable turn input this message was materialized from, present
when the input arrived through queued ingress and absent when the
turn was executed with its input in hand.

turn_id.description: The turn whose input this message carries.

oneOf.description:
A durable assistant output belonging to a turn. The source remains
typed so hosts can suppress their live row without parsing ids while
still recognizing protocol-owned output.

cell_id.description:
The executed cell this output is the assistant context of: the
[`crate::CellRecord::id`] of the cell the reply ran. `None` for
output that ran no cell.

source.description: The runtime or plugin that authored the output.

turn_id.description: The turn that produced this output.

ModelToolReturnPart.description:
One ordered block of a tool's model-facing result: text, an attachment
at the position the tool's value placed it, or output retained out of
history (FIG-1643). The same blocks travel unchanged into the
transcript's one [`crate::Part::ToolResult`] and the provider request's
one tool-result block.

oneOf.description:
Text too long for history, retained as a session attachment. A reader
of the result sees the witness as text; the reference is never
materialized into a request, so retention never expands a prompt.

reference.description: The session attachment holding the complete output.

witness.description: The bounded text history keeps in the output's place.

Name.description:
A variable, parameter or declared-function name.

Any text is a name; the kernel gives none of them meaning. Structural
validation refuses the empty name.

NamespaceFrontierRefusal.description: A frontier's refusal of a recorded resolution of one plugin's namespace.

NamespaceShadowing.description: The requested operation hidden by a lexical binding, independent of its type.

binding_origin.description:
The originating cell, when the resolution environment retains it.
Name-only session environments leave this absent.

NextRun.description:
The run spec a frame switch's follow-on runs under (FIG-6021), in its
serialized form. The spec type belongs to the store vocabulary above
this crate, which converts it both ways; the sans-io core carries it
unread. The producer of the switch states it whole: inheriting the
switching run's shape is passing that run's recorded spec back, and a
different spec is exactly that spec. The switch's commit mails the
follow-on under it, so every retry of that commit mails the same one.

OperationSlot.description:
Disjoint operation namespaces. Helper bodies retain their own local import
slots, but execution identifies their declarations by content.

OperationUse.description:
One authored import or helper operation declaration in one immutable Link.
All dispatch, modes, recorded reads and waited outcomes use this identity.

OwnerEpoch.description:
The owner's epoch: advances when ownership of the session or durable
process moves, so a message from a superseded owner is refused.

OwnerRevisionConflict.description: The planning revision refused under a still-current owner epoch.

PackageRefusal.description: Typed immutable-content and admission refusals shared by both backends.

PageRefusal.description:
Why the parent refused a page exchange. Every refusal ends the
activation as infrastructure; none is a guest outcome.

optional.description:
The argument may be omitted, and is then absent (`K-FN-004`). No
required parameter follows an optional one.

Part.description:
An ordered message part whose variant owns its kind-specific fields.
`id` identifies the part within its message; `content` is rendered text,
except on a tool result, whose content is its ordered blocks.
Serialization uses a flat object and rejects unknown fields and invalid
kind/field combinations through [`InvalidPartCombination`].

PayloadKind.description: A typed payload inside a frame that did not encode or decode.

oneOf.description:
Document position hints (`entered`, each task's last) alongside
exact statement-start count deltas (`ran`) since the previous frame.

PluginCallbackIdentity.description: A callback slot within one plugin, selected by its stable key.

oneOf.description: Two factories cannot own the same plugin namespace.
The declaration names another plugin than the factory that gave it.
The plugin cannot read the stream state its callbacks write.
The plugin cannot write the format it reads natively.

PluginFailureClass.description: How a declared plugin failure settles, independent of its display text.

PluginFailureOrigin.description: The declared code that produced a failure. Lash stamps this at dispatch.

PluginHookFailure.description: One failed callback in registration order, including its original typed payload.

PluginOperationFailure.description: A failure whose payload remains intact when its codec is unavailable.

oneOf.description: A built-in tool check selected one terminal reply over others.

A recorded resolution does not follow its namespace's applied
frontier: it skips a publication, or a predecessor publishes after
ownership moved on.

A reduced publication was abandoned before the engine returned it, so
whether it is durable is unknown: the namespace publishes nothing
more until it is rebuilt from durable state.

A callback returned commands where no recorded body can carry their
resolution.

PoolFault.description: A failure of the supervising pool itself, met while it drove a worker.

oneOf.description: A typed refusal of the native library held by a worker.

The host's cgroup v2 subtree cannot hold the pool's workers under
the limits it configured (FIG-6787).

ProcessChangeCursor.description:
Opaque position in a store's Process Change Feed.

The wrapped sequence is meaningful only to the registry backend that issued
it. Backends expose constructors/accessors so external store implementations
can persist and bind the position, but consumers should treat values as
cursors, not comparable timestamps.

ProcessDefinition.description:
One immutable definition as a holder sees it: its id and its signature.

Returned by create, get and publish with the derived signature. When a
value carries one back in, its signature is a claim that
`ProcessEngineRegistry::verify_definition_claim` checks.

ProcessDefinitionId.description:
The content-derived id of one immutable process definition.

Serializes as `{"$lash_definition_id": "<spelling>"}` and refuses any other
field on the way in. Ordering is over the spelling.

ProcessEnvRefusal.description:
Why a process environment is refused at admission (ADR 0004; D7, D10).
A refused environment stores nothing.

oneOf.description:
A new env names a component the deployment declares retired
(FIG-6296): only a sealed env may still name it.

A sealed env links an effect to a provider of a component the
deployment declares retired: every later call of it would have no
body.

A retired component published step state in the process: what its
later steps would read is gone.
The env does not link an effect the entry calls or spawns.
The env links an effect the entry never calls or spawns.
A linked tool does not fit the effect's kernel signature.
No env component serves a linked tool under its config.

A tool linked at a path a package owns does not serve the package's
operation (PKG-RUNNER).

The serving component serves a linked tool under another contract
than the process's code requires (`operation_contract_changed`).

Capture matched an effect to a tool of the run's recorded surface,
or of the declaring cell's committed deferred match, that no
component the env names serves.

Capture matched an effect to a tool the declaring cell's deferred
provider resolved, whose execution binding no component the env
names reads: its codec has no process twin there, or the twin does
not read the binding's format.
The document's linked-effect set could not be certified.
The engine refuses the engine settings the start states.

ProcessSignature.description:
A process signature as it travels on a value: a claim, never authority.

The engine's stored artifact decides what a definition's real signature is;
see [`ProcessEngine::resolve`](super::engine::ProcessEngine::resolve). Core
compares claim against authority and refuses a disagreement before any
durable row exists.

[`ProcessSignature::Unknown`] is how a holder says it asserts nothing
(ADR 0090's unknown process type). It is not a wildcard that matches: it is
the absence of a claim, so resolution adopts the authority outright. A
[`ProcessSignature::Known`] claim must equal the authority exactly.

ProcessStatus.description:
Durable lifecycle status of a process row.

This enum has no `#[serde(other)]` fallback arm, by design: a store that
silently folded an unknown status into a known one would corrupt the very
fold the registry exists to keep honest.

ProcessSuccessorRefusal.description:
Why a successor request is refused. A refusal records nothing, and the
process goes on as written.

oneOf.description: The new pair does not link (P1): items 17 and 21.

The new env links `effect`, which an admitted step of the process
performs, otherwise than the step's admission matched it.

The engine's own reason, as its data: for a kernel process, why no
correspondence carries its run onto the new document.

ProtocolBreach.description:
A parent, its worker or the pool between them broke the protocol. A fresh
worker may keep it, so the owning invocation is redriven.

oneOf.description: A checkpoint root the worker itself sealed fails the parent's check.
Worker code, or the parent task driving it, panicked.

ProtocolEvent.description:
Durable protocol payload stored in session history. Its payload is
shared by every clone of the event (see [`ProtocolPayload`]).

ProviderFailureKind.description:
Classification of a provider/transport failure.

This is the single canonical failure-kind vocabulary: provider transports
classify failures into it (`lash-core` re-exports it from
`llm::transport`), the turn machine carries it on
[`ErrorEnvelope`](crate::session_model::ErrorEnvelope), and hosts read it
back from `TurnIssue`s without scraping traces.

`Unknown` is an explicit classification, never a decoder fallback.
Persisted failure records reject unrecognized kind literals.

ProviderName.description: Logical owner/local provider identity, independent of the session/process hosting registry.

origin.description:
Exact LLM Provider route that minted this reasoning replay state.
Missing on sessions persisted before replay provenance was introduced.

Exact LLM Provider route that minted this opaque replay state. Missing
on sessions persisted before replay provenance was introduced.

ProviderRouteIdentity.description:
Stable identity of one configured LLM Provider route.

`endpoint` is either a normalized base URL or a host-supplied opaque route
id. Together with the LLM Provider kind and requested model it is the replay
contract. Model aliases behind one endpoint are intentionally out of scope:
hosts must use the exact model string they want included in route equality.
HTTP(S) endpoints reject userinfo because credentials are neither route
identity nor safe trace metadata. Explicit default ports remain distinct
from implicit ports. Scheme and host case, plus an empty path versus `/`,
normalize; path case and query strings remain identity-significant.

QualifiedName.description: An Import name parsed by segment, optionally addressing a type member.

ReasoningRefused.description:
A reasoning selection the recorded capability of the model under `key`
refuses.

ReasoningSelection.description: The host-resolved reasoning choice carried from model selection to providers.

oneOf.description: Send no reasoning control; the endpoint's own default applies.
Explicitly turn reasoning off, where the capability declares `disable`.
Request a named, capability-validated effort.

RecordRest.description: A record either refuses, discards, or retains undeclared fields.

rest.description: What happens to fields not named in `fields` at a boundary.

RecordedCallbackUnavailable.description: A recorded callback key the running build no longer registers.

ReferrerStore.description: The byte family a referrer claims.

oneOf.description:
The document, or the body of a library function it reaches, fails
structural validation (`K-DOC-005`), a call by name of a function
with no native implementation among them (`K-LIB-002`).
`K-ADM-001`: the environment provides no such effect.
`K-ADM-003`: the environment holds no function of this identity.

`K-FORM-003`: a variable is read or assigned where no enclosing scope
has declared it.

`K-ADM-005`: an argument can never be a value of its parameter's
type.

`K-ADM-006`: a `perform` states a result type no result of the
effect's signature can have.

RefusalSite.description: Where a config refusal was raised.

oneOf.description: One command of a transaction, by its position and registered name.

The candidate as a whole: a transaction's final candidate, or the
config a run's overrides derived.
The creation of the session's namespace.

RegistrationRefused.description:
Why registration refused a tool: why its manifest cannot be built, or why
a catalog does not take it.

oneOf.description:
The tool's manifest does not declare a bound its host must set: its
`execution`, or the `park` of a tool that may defer.
A tool that never defers declares a `park` bound it can never use.
The tool's declaration is itself invalid.
The tool is declared isolated and names no process engine to run in.
A tool that is not isolated names a process engine it never runs in.

The tool is isolated in a process engine its deployment does not
register: an isolated call never falls back to an inline body.

A tool defined with an output declares a turn control. A control
call has no output, so its contract states none: the control is its
result. [`ToolDefinition::control`] defines one.

A `Read` tool declares a capability a read never has: deferral,
intents, isolation or a turn control.

A `Read` tool's provider registered no reader: a read never falls
back to the provider's recorded execution.

RegistryKind.description: The registry a recorded callback resolves through.

oneOf.description: A session's plugins.
A process's environment components.

RenderRefusal.description:
Why a protocol refused to resolve the render a run's results present
with. `refusal` is the protocol's own refusal type, serialized, and
`message` its display text.

ReportedFailure.description:
A failure reported to hosts: the single payload both host lanes carry for
it (`SessionStreamEvent::Error` and the turn activity's `Error`).

envelope.description:
The failure's typed kind, code, terminal reason, retryability and
provider classification, when its source classified it.

ResponsePhase.description:
Provider replay phase tag: the two-value vocabulary the kernel interprets
(`"commentary"`/`"final_answer"` on the wire). An unknown spelling fails
decoding rather than silently meaning "neither".

origin.description:
Exact LLM Provider route that minted this provider-owned response
metadata. Missing on sessions persisted before replay provenance was
introduced.

provider_payload.description:
Provider-owned payload needed to replay this text part on a future
request. The kernel stores it opaquely and providers decide whether it
is valid for their next wire request.

RetainedOutput.description:
An output history does not hold: the attachment that holds its complete
bytes, and the bounded witness history keeps in its place.

The witness is what a reader of history — the model, a transcript — sees
of the output. It is never expanded automatically: the complete bytes are
read only by resolving `reference` through the session's attachment store.

reference.description: The session attachment holding the complete output.

witness.description: The bounded text history keeps in the output's place.

RetainedValue.description:
A code mode value retained out of history (FIG-1439): the retention of
its JSON encoding, and the shape of the value, which history keeps for a
program to read in its place.

RetiredProcessStatus.description:
The status a process row had when retention reclaimed it: the retired
subset of [`ProcessStatus`].

A tombstone and every "no longer retained" answer carry one, so a pruned
process still says how it ended: a `failed` one is never reported as
completed.

RetirementRefusal.description: A registry retirement refuses new admission or a recorded dependency.

RetryProgress.description:
A retry that is about to wait: the single payload the provider stream and
both host lanes carry for it (`LlmStreamEvent::RetryStatus`,
`SessionStreamEvent::RetryStatus` and the turn activity's `RetryStatus`).

envelope.description: The failure being retried, when its source classified it.

RunBound.description:
One of the bounds a run states and its worker pool admits up to: a
field of [`crate::RunBounds`].

RunCutRefusal.description:
Why a Run's frame cannot proceed: an earlier frame of its invocation
failed.

RunDefinitionRefusal.description:
Why a registered definition refused to shape a run: deterministic, so it
is recorded as the run's failure. `refusal` is the definition's own
refusal type, serialized, and `message` its display text.

RunId.description:
One logical Run: a turn or operation and every physical segment it owns.
Its spelling is retained across restart and redrive.

RunInput.description: An input of the run that the worker reads when it starts.

RunRefusal.description:
The run's own inputs are refused. They are the same on every attempt, so
redriving the invocation refuses them again: the refusal is terminal.

oneOf.description: A cache miss must name code supplied under this exact run's ownership.
The run names immutable code the worker's exact image does not own.

The run's session or process recorded a dialect this worker's
embedding does not install: the host that built the worker did not
name it. Refused before the document is read or anything runs.

The worker will not resume the checkpoint: its pinned
release, a function or native it needs, or a wait's admission.

The document is not admitted, names a library function the worker
has not registered, or has no such entry.
The parked run is not one this machine resumes.

The run asks for more of a bound than its worker pool admits
(FIG-6827): the pool's run bounds are a ceiling, never a clamp.
Refused before anything runs.

RunShapeRefusal.description:
Why a run's shape was refused: deterministic, so it is the run's
recorded failure, carried typed as
[`RuntimeErrorCause::RunShapeRefused`](crate::RuntimeErrorCause::RunShapeRefused).

oneOf.description: The spec's registered definition refused its context.

A config owner refused the config the run's overrides derived, or
the options the run stated for it.

The reasoning the run would run is one its model's recorded
capability refuses.
The spec sets a reasoning selection for a session with no model.
The protocol refused to resolve the run's render.

RuntimeEffectReplayMismatchReport.description: Compact, content-free mismatch evidence retained on the controller error.

effect_kind.description:
The kind of the recorded effect whose envelope diverged (its command
`type`, e.g. `llm_call`, `tool_invocation`), so an operator can tell a
model-call drift from a tool or cell drift (FIG-3587).

RuntimeErrorCause.description:
Typed cause retained when a controller-owned runtime effect must abort
through the generic runtime error boundary.

Attachment retention and worker causes keep their source's retry class.
Other causes are terminal except for an unavailable recorded model.

oneOf.description: The owner still holds its epoch, but its draft has an older revision.
Typed linked-content or execution-membership refusal.
The deployment retired a registry entry a session still needs.
A host-configured aggregate callback deadline passed without an answer.
Recorded material could not be read. This cause grants no body retry.

A callback returned state commands where no recorded body carries
their resolution.
A recorded callback's published state belongs to another owner.

A recorded state resolution does not follow its namespace's applied
frontier.

A namespace holds a reduced publication of unknown durability; it
publishes nothing more until the owner is rebuilt from durable state.
The attempt is not recorded: the invocation's recovery owns it.

A plugin's own key, size or codec refusal of its namespace, such as
a readiness hook that cannot decode a value it reads (FIG-5324).
A completed provider call's refusal, retained through plugin and host errors.
A typed worker failure retained through protocol and host errors.

The VM state a stopped code cell resumes from is refused by this
build's worker: another build wrote it. Nothing of the cell is
recorded for it, and it is no outcome of the cell: its turn parks on
the cell's snapshot, and a build that reads the state resumes it
(FIG-5613).
A process start names a scope whose lifetime has closed.

A process environment was refused at admission, or a start named
one that is not published (FIG-6034).
A host start key already names a different start.
The attachment-store family and structured source of a required retention failure.

The identity of a submission refused for using another ingress kind's
reserved source-key namespace.

A send named an id its session forsook: the host closed the id
before lash saw an input under it, and no input is ever admitted
under it ([`RuntimeErrorCode::TurnInputForsaken`]).
A durable record cannot be decoded. Retrying cannot repair its bytes.
A process row lacks the configuration its engine requires to execute.

A Lash object's compatibility record, or its absence, refuses this
build (ADR 0115 §3.2): the typed half of
[`RuntimeErrorCode::EngineObjectStateFormatUnsupported`] when the
refusal is the object's, not one stored value's.

An artifact publish or acquire named a referrer that has a fence
(ADR 0113 §2.7): the typed half of
[`RuntimeErrorCode::ArtifactReferrerEnded`].

The recorded model key this worker could not bind (FIG-4404).
A deployment serving the key repairs this retryable cause.

A tool call passed the session's recorded `max_tool_calls`
(FIG-4546): the typed half of
[`RuntimeErrorCode::MaxToolCallsExceeded`].

Why a run's shape was refused (FIG-4652): the typed half of
[`RuntimeErrorCode::RunShapeRefused`] and, for a refused reasoning,
of [`RuntimeErrorCode::ReasoningRefused`].

Why the config a session's creation stated was refused (FIG-4652):
the typed half of [`RuntimeErrorCode::SessionConfigRefused`].

RuntimeOwner.description:
Who a runtime runs for: a session, or a process named by its minted id.

A session runtime and a process runtime cross the same interfaces — the
plugin session, the tool catalog, the attachment facade, the authority a
tool intent is declared under — and those interfaces take a
`RuntimeOwner`. A process runtime is never handed a session id as a
stand-in for its own identity.

SIGNATURE_REQUIRED.description:
Only entry promotion requires a written parameter and settled-result type.
Producers resolve explicit any/unknown to Json before calling this seam.

oneOf.description:
A composition whose members no kernel type states, or whose meet
grows past the projection's bound
([`crate::schema::MAX_PROJECTED_TYPE_NODES`]), at the JSON
pointer `schema_path`: a value of the schema could not be typed.

ScopeId.description:
A scope a process may live until.

An effect opener (a logical turn run, a session operation, one process)
or a session. A session is never a tool Run opener:
it owns lifetimes, not effects.

oneOf.description: An effect opener's scope.
A session's scope, closed when the session is deleted.

SequenceFault.description:
A message that arrived out of order, or an exchange whose accounting does
not add up.

SessionAppendNode.description:
Typed node accepted at session-graph append boundaries.

Its semantic fields are projected by Lash's versioned append-request
identity encoder. Adding or changing a variant or nested semantic field
requires an identity encoding version bump and replacement golden corpus;
serde representation itself is deliberately not the identity format.

SessionHeadOwner.description: What owns a session's head, refusing a head write outside every run.

oneOf.description: An admitted run without terminal evidence.
The session actor currently holds its grant.
An open session command, the earliest by `enqueue_seq`.

Signature.description: What a function, an effect or an entry takes and returns.

SignatureMismatch.description:
The first incompatible part found by the signature's serving relation.
`path` uses JSON pointer escaping in the projected type structure:
`/input`, `/output`, and their properties, items or additional properties.
The types are the kernel's projections, not the original JSON schemas.

SignatureSide.description: The side of an effect signature that cannot serve its declaration.

Site.description:
A node's address: the code it belongs to and the chain of
[`Node::children`] indexes that reaches it from that code's body.

A site is derived from the document and is never written by a host
(`K-ID-004`). An empty chain addresses the body itself.

Span.description: UTF-8 byte offsets in authored or printed source.

StartKey.description:
The idempotency key of one process start (ADR 0107).

A start key is never a reference: nothing resolves a key to a process. The
registrar maps a key to the process it minted for it while that process is
retained, so a retried start returns the retained process instead of
starting a second one, and after the process is pruned the same key starts
a new process with a new id.

A key lash derives from an admitted operation (a tool intent, an isolated
call) is trusted: a retry under it returns the retained process
whatever it submitted. A host's key (one it supplied, or its keyless
start's derived key) fences its start: a retry under it returns the
retained process only if it presents the same start, and is otherwise a
[`StartKeyConflict`](crate::runtime_error::RuntimeErrorCode::ProcessStartKeyConflict)
that names nothing but the key.

Every key is a framed digest in one family, with each start path in its own
namespace, so a host-supplied key can never collide with one lash derives
for a tool intent or isolated call. The digest is over admitted
operation identity only — never over submitted content, source or compiler
identity, or the minted result. Only [`StartKey::for_host`] is open to a
host; every other family is derived under a [`StartKeyDerivation`].

StatementForm.description:
An action form, as a refusal names one the body of a function with a
native implementation may not run (`K-LIB-004`).

StoreFault.description:
A fault of the storage substrate that stays typed past the store, with
the same fields as its store error. A plugin error is cloned and
journaled, so it carries this rather than the store error: the identical
operation may succeed when it is made again, and nothing about it is the
operation's answer.

oneOf.description: Another writer holds the backend's write authority.
Another connection holds a database a whole-store migration needs.
The substrate failed the operation before it returned a value.
A backend failure with no typed cause.

StoreRefusal.description:
A store refusal that stays typed past the store, with the same fields as
its store error: a compatibility, session identity or cancellation
authority refusal. Plugin errors are cloned and journaled, so
this representation carries only the terminal refusals rather than backend
failures and sources.

oneOf.description: The immutable window selected by a run is no longer retained.

StreamBlockEvent.description:
One step of a streamed output block's lifecycle: the single payload every
lane carries for it — the provider stream, the session stream, turn
activity and the trace. A lane adds its own envelope (observation
identity, correlation, sequence, elapsed time) around this payload and
never redefines it.

oneOf.description: The next suffix of `block`'s text.

`block` closed. `text` is the block's authoritative text, so a
consumer can correct drift from accumulated deltas.

StreamBlockIdentity.description:
Provider-minted identity of one streamed output block.

Minted by the provider adapter from provider facts: OpenAI
`(item_id, summary_index)`, Anthropic content-block index, or a
deterministic per-attempt ordinal for providers with no native notion.
The id is opaque to hosts; ordering comes from `ordinal`, never from
parsing `id`. Live and replayed streams emit identical identities.

id.description: Opaque provider-minted block key, stable within one response attempt.

item_id.description:
The reasoning or message item this block belongs to, when the provider
has one. N blocks may share one item's replay material.

ordinal.description: Per-attempt block ordinal assigned by the provider adapter.

StreamBlockKind.description:
Which render lane a streamed output block belongs to.

A *block* is the unit a host renders: one OpenAI reasoning summary part,
one Anthropic `thinking`/`text` content block, or one ordinal run of
thought/text for providers with no native notion. Blocks name their owning
reasoning item or message item when the provider has one; several blocks
may share one item's replay material.

oneOf.description: Visible assistant prose.

Reasoning summary ("thinking") text, kept separate from assistant
response text.

StreamStateFormatRefusal.description: Opaque stream-hook state whose format the receiving plugin cannot read.

SupervisorEvidence.description:
What the supervisor observed of a worker's end. Evidence, never testimony:
a worker cannot claim how it ended.

oneOf.description: The pipe closed with no exit status observed yet.

The worker made a system call its confinement does not allow, and
the kernel killed it (`SIGSYS`).

SurfaceCollision.description:
Two tools a surface would offer as one operation: refused, naming both
tools and both providers. The host fixes it by reconfiguring one
provider.

SurfaceDuplicateTool.description: A surface entry whose tool id another entry already offers.

SurfaceRefusal.description: Why a surface could not be built.

ToolBound.description:
The bound a tool's manifest must declare, named by
[`RegistrationRefused::MissingBound`].

oneOf.description: [`ToolManifest::execution`], which every tool declares.
[`ToolManifest::park`], which every tool that may defer declares.

ToolCallLimitExceeded.description:
A tool call refused by the session's [`MaxToolCalls`]: the program asked
for more tool calls than its recorded limit admits.

It is the program's failure, never the host's: the limit is recorded
config and the count is a fact of the program's own history, so a replay
or a redrive refuses the same call. Nothing of the refused calls is
journaled or dispatched.

counted.description:
The calls counted against the limit before the refused ones: made so
far by a cell, held now by a process.

limit.description: The recorded `max_tool_calls` the execution runs under.

requested.description:
The calls refused together: one for a single call, an aggregate's
unique tool calls for an aggregate.

oneOf.description: A cell: the limit is the total it may make.
A process: the limit is what it may hold at once.

projection_value.description: Optional display projection for a successful result; `outcome` remains the code value.

forced.description:
Whether lash forced the end: a cancelled process whose engine did not
end it within its cancel grace (ADR 0132 §10).

oneOf.description: A tool's operation is no canonical operation.
The tool supplied no output type, including the empty schema.
Two tools are performed as one operation.
A member is refused against the deployment it registers in.

ToolCheckConflict.description:
The terminal reply a tool check's reduction selected and every terminal
reply it displaced, in reduction order.

ToolCheckPhase.description: The built-in tool check phase a reply was given in.

ToolCheckReply.description: One callback's reply to a tool check, attributed to its plugin.

ToolCheckVerdictKind.description: What a tool check callback decided, without the decision's payload.

oneOf.description:
A turn-ending control the tool declared
([`TurnControls`](lash_kernel_value::tool_declaration::TurnControls)): the call's whole result.

A plugin's tool check stopped the owning logical Run (ADR 0128). The
call's outcome carries the failure the model reads; this is the Run
control, under the aborting plugin's namespaced code.
A workflow entry's supplied input or settled result violates its contract.
An effect answer violates its declared result type.
A host-configured aggregate callback deadline passed without an answer.

The host body panicked. It may already have performed outside work;
this terminal is never retried or sent back to the model for repair.

An admitted engine step has no registered body on this deployment.
Its exact registration refusal is retained in the failure's raw value.
A body for an engine step was requested for a non-engine process.

A result check proposed state commands outside the recorded body
that owns its decision. No command was reduced or published.

The body's outcome is one its recorded declaration does not admit: a
Deferred without `may_defer`, an undeclared intent kind, or an
undeclared turn control. Nothing
the outcome declared was realized.

A start the body declared names an environment its attempt did not
hold through `AttemptContext::declare_launch` (D10). Nothing the
outcome declared was realized.

A process step's linked tool is missing from the provider its env
links it to on this node (D3). The body did not run.

A call's linked tool is served on this node under another contract
id than the call is pinned to (`operation_contract_changed`). The
body did not run.

A granted tool's transform refused the tool's input: it names no
call. Nothing was resolved.

A computed target or returned alias entered a statically linked
package namespace. No target tool ran.

A process's call of a tool its env links as a dispatch grant that
the deferred provider's registration on this node does not grant:
only a granted tool dispatches. Nothing was resolved.

A granted tool's transform, run again for the call of the matched
tool, named another call path than the committed match resolved: the
transform is not deterministic, a host bug. The matched tool did not
run.

No tool is available for the call path a granted tool's transform
named, with the host's note. The decision is recorded and never
resolved again; no tool ran.

A control call made from a task the cell spawned. Only the cell's
main task ends the turn; the body did not run.

A control call made while a task the cell started is outstanding or
its result unobserved. The body did not run.

The iteration's one control attempt is spent: an earlier control
call was already admitted. The body did not run.

A call beside this control call in its round failed or was
cancelled, so the turn does not end on it. The body did not run.

A workflow's body ended in an error no `catch` took (FIG-6810). The
failure's message is the error's own message, and its raw value the
error's data: for a failed tool call, the tool's failure.

error_kind.description:
The error's kind as the body raised it (`type_error`,
`tool_failed`), or `None` when the body threw a value that is
not an error.

site.description:
Where the run's main task raised it, in the document the process
runs: the `perform`, `sleep` or `join` whose outcome raised, else
the statement whose evaluation raised, a library call's included.
An error out of library code, an `await` of a failed task's among
them, names the first document statement it unwinds into, and one
a `finally` held names its `try` statement. `None` when a run-root
cleanup held it (a Python entry that started tasks), or no
document statement was left to name it.

ToolIntentActivityOutcome.description: The new fact a tool intent produced, without copying its committed process record.

ToolIntentCommandFailure.description: The typed command cause retained by a tool intent and carried to the host.

oneOf.description: A package port refusal or infrastructure failure retains its typed cause.
A provider refusal retains the host's classification and namespaced code.
A process cannot run without the behaviour its creation recorded.
The process already accepted a different cancellation request.

A new start named a closed scope: its starter has ended, or the scope
its lifetime names has closed (FIG-3607 R11). The start is refused
before an id is minted, so the refusal names the start by its key.

A host start key is bound to a retained process another start made
(ADR 0107): the retry presented a different start. A host key is
global, so the retained process may be another originator's; the
refusal names the key and nothing of the process it is bound to.

A process environment was refused at admission, or a start named one
that is not published (FIG-6034). A retry meets it again.

A host's successor request for a process was refused (FIG-6121, D2):
nothing was recorded, and the process goes on as written.
An installed package's namespace is closed to deferred resolution.
OP-INTERNAL: document code cannot resolve a package-private operation.
Discovery must itself be an inline member of the tool catalogue.
A protocol's per-call batch maximum exceeds its hard ceiling.

An execution mode's tool presenter refused: the host's presentation
config at a session's creation, or a section it could not present.
`presenter` is the installed presenter id; `code` is its stable, dotted
cause kind. `message` carries human-readable details.
An effective resident catalog member could not supply its immutable definition.

A catalog member's declared execution is refused against the runtime's
execution budgets: an inline-only tool declared above the ceiling.

The tools a run's providers advertise under its config do not build
into one surface: two share a model-facing name, or a tool id. The
host reconfigures one provider.

A fresh session create named an id the catalog already holds. A
create never adopts an existing session (FIG-4112); replaying a
recorded identity is a process run's `SessionTurn` initialisation,
not a create.

A lane-less head write found an owner in the store transaction.
Submit host head writes as boundary session commands, or retry once
the owner releases the head. The refused write changes nothing.
A plugin's config registration cannot stand on the deployment's plugin set.
An atomic plugin-state refusal, retained across journal transport.

A factory's [`super::PluginDeclaration`] failed the composition's owner
and format checks (FIG-4732): a session cannot materialize under a
plugin set that misstates itself, before any plugin callback runs.
A typed linked-content or execution-use refusal from the store.
A store compatibility refusal, preserved through plugin-facing ports.

The storage substrate faulted under a plugin-facing port: the identical
operation may succeed when it is made again, and nothing about the
fault is the operation's answer.

An existing plugin session cannot be reconstructed because a required
protocol-owned field is absent from its durable record.
A host attempted to substitute a durably pinned protocol selection.

A turn-scoped plugin write presented a lapsed or superseded borrowed
session-execution guard.
A session append operation id was reused for different semantic request content.

operation_key.description: Canonical durable operation key that was reused incorrectly.

session_id.description: Session whose append operation identity conflicted.

oneOf.description:
Durable append receipt metadata contradicts the retry's requested-node
count. This is store corruption, not a caller-recoverable conflict.

operation_key.description: Canonical durable operation key of the corrupt receipt.

session_id.description: Session whose append receipt is corrupt.

oneOf.description:
A durable plugin-owned record contained a value outside its declared
representation. Retrying cannot repair the stored bytes.

message.description: Backend diagnostic describing the malformed field or payload.

record_kind.description: Stable name of the durable record whose payload was unreadable.

oneOf.description:
A backend-owned authoritative clock produced a value before the Unix
epoch, outside the runtime clock contract.

A session-only operation ran under a process runtime. A process has
no session and no agent frame of its own, and is never handed its
originator's session as a stand-in.

An external or host completion named a stored attachment that has no
upload evidence: its source was ended and swept, so the output would
reference bytes nothing can read. Nothing is recorded.
An operation referenced a process id that the registry never knew.
A roster continuation was reused with a different selection.

A Process Change Feed cursor predates deletion history removed by
Tombstone Compaction. The consumer must perform a full relist before
resuming from the reported horizon.

A read of one process's events starts below the prefix its host released
(`release_process_events`). The events at or below the horizon keep
their sequence and replay identity but no longer carry their payload;
the reader resumes after the reported horizon.

released_through.description: The highest released sequence: reads resume strictly after it.

oneOf.description:
A recovery would end a process that a later segment already carries
(FIG-3820).

A process-registry continuation was passed to a backend other than the
backend that issued it.

ToolIntentIdentity.description:
Generates the canonical tool-intent kind set from the vocabulary in
[`crate::tool_intents`].

execution_scope_id.description:
The enclosing execution-scope id: a turn id for turn scope and a
process id for process scope.

minting_emission_replay_key.description:
Replay key of the durable invocation that minted this declaration,
retained so `replay_key` stays re-derivable from the record alone.
`None` for host-submitted intents, whose identity binds no emission.

owner.description:
The runtime whose authority declared the intent: a session, or a
process runtime.

ToolIntentKind.description:
Literal command kind of one recorded declaration.

Generated from [`tool_intent_variants!`]; never hand-edited.

ToolIntentRealizedRef.description: The typed identity and admission outcome of a realized intent.

oneOf.description: The signature is the definition admission's new outcome, alongside its id.

The logical Run whose emission minted this intent is cancel-decided:
ADR 0099 §4 forbids new semantic admission under a cancelled
invocation, so the intent is refused before any of its commands run.

A declared start whose identity is not the one its call's declaring
attempt derives for index 0 (ADR 0116 §3.1): another call's, another
execution scope's or minting emission's, a nonzero index, or a replay
key its own fields do not derive. `expected` is the identity the
runtime derived from the admitted call; `recorded` is the one the
declaration carried. Nothing was registered.

ToolIntentRuntimeFailure.description:
The durable fields of a runtime command failure. Invocation-local retry
markers are not recorded command facts.

ToolProviderHandle.description: The scoped address of a declared provider. Only the callback codec spells its seam prefix.

TransportSequence.description:
The transport sequence: each direction numbers its messages from zero,
one apart, so a dropped, duplicated or reordered message is refused.

TurnActivityId.description:
Stable identifier for a semantic turn activity.

An activity a shift observation yields is named by the observation's
replay key and ordinal, `{key}#{ordinal}`; a frame of coalesced stream
deltas is named by the ordinal range it covers, `{key}#{first}..{last}`
(FIG-5098). Both re-derive identically on a redrive, which is what lets a
live replay store drop what it already delivered. Any other id is opaque.

oneOf.description: End the turn with `value`.

value_schema.description:
The schema `value` was checked against when its call settled: the
admitted declaration's ([`FinishDeclaration`](lash_kernel_value::tool_declaration::FinishDeclaration)).
A body's own Finish states none; settlement stamps it, and every
later reader — a completion candidate, a replay, a batch that
folds the call — keeps the schema the value settled under rather
than reading a live one.

oneOf.description:
End the turn by switching to a fresh agent frame that starts on
`task` with `initial_nodes`, its follow-on running under `next_run`.

TurnControlKind.description: A way a tool's call may end its caller's turn.

oneOf.description: The turn ends with the value the call carries.
The turn ends by switching to a fresh agent frame.

TurnInputAcceptanceReceipt.description:
Durable acceptance evidence returned to an ingress caller.

The receipt deliberately carries only stable routing and idempotency
identity. Queue dispatch and the pending row's mutable lifecycle state are
observed separately through the pending-input reconciliation surface.

TurnInputApplication.description:
Durable evidence that an admitted input became canonical conversation input.

This is the application stage between [`TurnInputAcceptanceReceipt`]
(admission) and the terminal turn commit (settlement). It deliberately
carries identity only: hosts correlate an input to its canonical turn and
committed message without parsing or retaining display text.

checkpoint.description:
Present for active-turn checkpoint application and absent when the
input formed the initial canonical input of an idle queued turn.

oneOf.description: Every value.

Every value `Any` admits that holds no closure, function reference,
dialect token holding one, task or handle anywhere in it: data, as a
JSON-schema slot describes it (`K-EFF-002`). It serves where `Any` is
expected; `Any` does not serve where it is.

An integer or a float. In an effect's result this is the bare number
the document's number policy decodes (`K-EFF-006`).
A tuple of exactly these member types.
A text that is one of these.
A closure or a function reference that takes and returns these.
A task handle whose task ends with this.
A handle of this host kind.
A value of any one of these types. Two or more, none itself a union.

TypeMismatch.description:
The first incompatible value at a public boundary. `path` is an RFC 6901
pointer into the value, never a path through the type grammar.

actual.description: A bounded kind witness; no user value is included.

Unit.description: The code a node belongs to.

oneOf.description: The document's `main`.
A declared function of the document.

The kernel-code body of an authored or build-owned library function.
Nested helper closures retain this owning identity and their site path.

ValueShape.description:
What a JSON value is made of. A position that held several values — the
elements of an array — is their merge: its sizes are the largest
observed, an object key not every one of them held is `optional`, and a
position whose values differ in type is [`ValueShape::OneOf`] them.

bytes.description: The string's length in UTF-8 bytes.

items.description:
The shape of the elements; absent for an empty array and for one
whose contents the bound counts.

fields.description: The described keys, in the order first observed.

omitted.description: Keys the bound counted instead of describing.

oneOf.description:
Values of more than one type, one shape per type in the order first
observed.

VersionRange.description: The wire form of [`VersionRange`], before validation.

WorkerDeploymentFault.description: Why this deployment cannot launch its configured worker executable.

WorkerFrameKind.description: The worker message an encoder refused, without its guest data.

WorkerLibraryRefusal.description: The native library's typed validation refusal, independent of VM transport.

oneOf.description: A build's generated helper plan has no exact body in the held image.

WorkerLimit.description: The VM or worker limit a run exhausted.

oneOf.description:
A step's execution observations outgrew the run's heap budget, which
bounds the stream a worker holds and hands its parent, or a single
observation outgrew what one frame carries (FIG-4458).
The encoded effect request or result exceeds its configured bound.
A parked run exceeds its configured bound.
A worker message cannot fit in one transport frame.

The execution's CPU time passed its configured budget: the parent's
cumulative accounting across the execution's attempts, or the CPU
ceiling the worker set from that budget (`SIGXCPU`).

One exchange computed or serialized past its configured wall-clock
deadline.

The worker's resident memory passed the `memory.max` of the cgroup
its host placed it in, and the kernel killed it (FIG-6787).

The execution held its workers past its configured wall time: the
sum over its checkouts, and for a code-mode cell over its
activations, of the time from a worker's admission to its release
(FIG-6786).
The execution spent its configured replacement attempts.

The host took longer than its configured host-read deadline to
answer one read (a clock, random, projection or planned-read answer,
or a limiter's decision) while the run held its worker. A durable
park releases its worker and has no such bound.

description:
App-facing semantic activity emitted during a turn.

`id` is unique per emitted activity event. `correlation_id` groups related
events in the same logical activity, such as code start/completion, tool
start/completion, or text deltas from one output block.

oneOf.description:
Announces the admitted logical run and physical turn identities before
any other activity from that turn.

Hosts use this identity for exact cancellation and steering targets;
they must not infer it from whichever incidental activity happens to
arrive first. Session-observation envelopes also carry `turn_id`, but
the payload keeps it available to turn-local and collected streams.

run_id.description: The committed admission identity hosts use to follow the run.

oneOf.description:
The checkpoint for this protocol iteration was recorded. All earlier
deltas on this turn's live lane precede that checkpoint.

One step of a streamed assistant-text or reasoning block: the same
payload the session stream, the provider stream and the trace carry.
Hosts render one block per streamed unit — an OpenAI reasoning summary
part, an Anthropic content block, or an ordinal run for providers with
no native notion. The activity's `correlation_id` names the block
within its model call's stream.

Marks a provider generation boundary before a retry and retracts any
visible text emitted by the superseded attempt.

Observers remove only prose and reasoning deltas whose correlation ids
appear here. The reset is itself replayed in order, so reconnecting
observers converge on the same visible text as live observers. Empty
correlation lists mean the provider regenerated before emitting visible
output; they remain boundary evidence and never mean "retract all."

A sealed per-call attempt ledger, including provider-reported evidence.

Observation only. Hosts meter each attempt at the Provider seam:
its returned Ok or Err, or attempt_ended when no result returned
(ADR 0127). A call whose cell was accepted mid-stream is recorded
when its tail drains.
The live cell return, retractable until its owning commit (ADR 0122).

duration_ms.description: The observed invocation window, absent when unmeasured.

language.description: Provisional activity, not yet committed and never committed after an Immediate stop (ADR 0122).

prints.description: Provisional activity, not yet committed and never committed after an Immediate stop (ADR 0122); absent when unavailable.

prints_retained.description: Provisional activity, not yet committed and never committed after an Immediate stop (ADR 0122).

result.description: Provisional activity, not yet committed and never committed after an Immediate stop (ADR 0122).

tool_call_ids.description: Provisional activity, not yet committed and never committed after an Immediate stop (ADR 0122); absent when unavailable.

oneOf.description: The owning commit accepted this cell and its outcome.

duration_ms.description: The observed invocation window, absent when unmeasured.

graph_key.description:
Graph key of the enclosing code block, when this tool call ran
inside one. `None` when the call did not run inside a code block.

provider_call_id.description: The model provider's id for the call, when a model issued it.

oneOf.description: The live tool return. Retractable until its outcome commits (ADR 0122).

duration_ms.description: The observed call window, absent when unmeasured.

graph_key.description:
Graph key of the enclosing code block, when this tool call ran
inside one. `None` when the call did not run inside a code block.

provider_call_id.description: The model provider's id for the call, when a model issued it.

oneOf.description: The accepted commit holds this outcome, including Interrupted on recovery.

duration_ms.description: The observed call window, absent when unmeasured.

graph_key.description:
Graph key of the enclosing code block, when this tool call ran
inside one. `None` when the call did not run inside a code block.

provider_call_id.description: The model provider's id for the call, when a model issued it.

oneOf.description: A declared Finish control ended the turn with `value`.

A retry that is about to wait, with the failure being retried: the
session stream's `RetryStatus` payload.

A reported failure with its typed envelope: the session stream's
`Error` payload.
